item.title: ECG Lab: An Interactive Electrocardiogram Learning Platform
item.description:
Project Background

ECG interpretation is a core clinical skill, but traditional learning methods often rely on static images and lengthy text, presenting several pain points:

  • 📱 Grid lines are hard to see on mobile devices, making waveform measurement difficult
  • 📚 Practice and learning are disconnected, with no immediate feedback after studying theory
  • 🎯 Emergency procedures can only be memorized through videos, lacking interactive training

ECG Lab was created to solve these problems.

Core Features

📚 Systematic Learning

  • 238 chapters: Covering electrophysiology, leads & vectors, atrial/ventricular hypertrophy, ischemia & infarction, electrolytes & medications, and more
  • Interactive ECG waveforms: 500 Hz sampling rate, supporting rhythm strips/12-lead display, loop/continuous scrolling, annotation and hover measurement
  • Bilingual support: All content available in Chinese and English

✍️ Practice Exercises

  • Systematic interpretation training: Six-step reading (rate→rhythm→axis→intervals→ST-T→conclusion) with step-by-step feedback
  • 2000+ practice questions: Covering 42 diagnoses, with chapter filtering and multi-select support
  • Three game modes: Classic interpretation, Speed 60s, Combo survival
  • Adaptive spaced repetition: Error log tracks confused options, with 1→3→8→20 day intervals

🎯 Simulation Tests

  • ACLS emergency simulation: 12 server-side state machine scenarios, CPR quality, defibrillation/cardioversion, drug timing training
  • ECG viewer: Supports zoom, measurement and annotation, analyzing real ECGs like in clinical practice

🔬 Laboratory

  • Cardiac Vector Lab: P/QRS/T 3D vector loops, hexaxial and limb lead projections, precordial lead positioning
  • Electrolyte Lab: K⁺/Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ sliders with real-time waveform changes
  • Daily Challenge: 10 site-wide questions, continuous check-in calendar

Tech Stack

Backend

  • PHP 8.4 (no framework, native implementation)
  • MySQL 8+
  • PDO MySQL
  • AES-256-GCM tokens
  • WebAuthn Passkey

Frontend

  • Native ES Modules (zero build tools)
  • Canvas / SVG waveform rendering
  • Service Worker (PWA offline support)

Highlights

  • Zero build for frontend and backend, no webpack/vite dependencies
  • Teaching-first design, all waveforms marked as “educational illustrations”
  • BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) AI integration support

Project Highlights

🎨 Interactive Design

Traditional ECG learning is “look at pictures and talk”, ECG Lab lets you operate hands-on:

  • Drag sliders to change electrolyte concentrations, observe waveform changes in real-time
  • Click anywhere on the waveform to measure intervals and amplitudes
  • Rotate 3D cardiac vector loops to understand spatial projections

📊 Intelligent Assessment

  • XP level system: Lv.1-20, unlocking different difficulty levels
  • Ability radar chart: Visualize mastery of each chapter
  • Error analysis: AI explains differential points for wrong options (unlocked at Lv.10)

🌍 Open Source & Free

  • Code licensed under MIT
  • Educational content under CC BY-SA 4.0
  • Full access without login required

User Experience

🔗 Live Demo: ecg.tianhao.me

  • Desktop and mobile responsive
  • PWA installable to home screen, offline capable
  • Dual themes (light/dark), Chinese/English interface switching

Project Screenshots

System learning interface: Course map and chapter navigation

Interactive waveforms: Zoom, measure, annotate

Cardiac Vector Lab: 3D vector loop visualization

Future Roadmap

  • 📱 WFDB/SCP format adaptation for real ECG data
  • 🎓 CME (Continuing Medical Education) assessment system
  • 🤖 Enhanced AI tutor supporting more clinical scenario Q&A
  • 📊 Waveform annotator for custom key point marking

Summary

ECG Lab is my exploration in medical education, attempting to solve traditional ECG learning pain points with modern web technologies. The project uses a zero-build native tech stack, focusing on interactivity and teaching experience, hoping to provide medical students and clinicians with an efficient and engaging learning tool.

Welcome to try it and provide feedback!

Repository: github.com/AndroidOL/ecg-academy
Live Site: ecg.tianhao.me

item.title: My Smart Assistant 2.0: Giving the "Lazy" Photography System a Panoramic Window
item.description:
It’s been a while since I last shared my “lazy” photography system—the one that decides when to snap a photo and when to chill. This little helper has been quietly working for me all this time. But as time went on, a new pain point emerged: while its inner workings were smart, the way I interacted with it remained… primitive.

Project code: https://github.com/AndroidOL/camera-capture/tree/main/web-ui

From “Command Line Archaeology” to “Tap of a Finger”: A Revolution in Experience

In the past, every interaction with the system felt like digital archaeology inside a server:

  • Want to see yesterday’s shots? Fire up your SSH client, connect to the server, and navigate through a maze of directories with cd and ls.
  • Want to tweak sensitivity settings? Use Vim or Nano to edit config files, save, and systemctl restart—then cross your fingers you didn’t miss a comma.

This was cumbersome and emotionally distant. My smart assistant—its joys, its output—was locked behind the black box of a terminal.

So I opened a window for it: a wide panoramic floor-to-ceiling window in the form of a web control console, designed for intuitive, elegant interaction—even from the comfort of a couch.

Now, everything has changed:

  • Open a browser and enter the local address;
  • A beautiful and powerful interface appears;
  • The once-silent background photographer now has a vivid “face” and nimble “hands.”

Its components:

  • Eyes: A real-time monitor with zero delay.
  • Hands: Clickable button menus for full control.
  • Brain: Complex logic wrapped in an intuitive design.

Four Superpowers of the Web Console

1. Time Drawer: A Tiered Photo Archive

Inspired by real-life “drawers,” navigating photos now feels like opening a set of Russian nesting dolls:

  1. Year/Month view: See all months with recordings.
  2. Daily preview: Thumbnail grid for each date.
  3. Hourly drawers: Tap to reveal 24-hour distributions.
  4. Minute-level access: Dig down to individual images.

Browsing becomes light, fun, and ceremonial.

2. Real-Time Window: A Watchful, Never-Blinking Guardian

Tap “Live Monitor,” and the system enters watch mode:

  • Heartbeat refresh: The frontend fetches a new frame every 2.5 seconds.
  • Auto-reconnect: Camera outages are self-healed.
  • Night mode: Auto-dimming for dark environments—no eye strain.

3. Time Tunnel: Your Personal Documentary Generator

The “Slideshow” mode is my favorite feature:

  • Select any date range (e.g., “2025 Cherry Blossom Season”);
  • The system stitches together all relevant photos into a dynamic time-lapse.

Highlights:

  • Slide mode: Chronologically ordered playback.
  • Smooth transitions: Fade-in/out between shots.
  • Timestamp overlay: Auto-displayed capture time at the bottom.

🎞️ I used this to relive the cherry blossom bloom—from bud to fall—utterly moving and magical.

4. Thoughtful Themes: A Smart and Caring Interface

As a night owl, I added a theme toggle:

  • Day mode: Blue-white for clarity.
  • Night mode: Deep black and crimson for eye comfort.
  • Auto-memory: Remembers your last-used theme.

Like a friend who just gets you.

Dev Diary: Humanizing the System, One Mishap at a Time

The Midnight Panic

One night while debugging live view, the screen started flashing like crazy!
Turned out I mistakenly set 250ms instead of 2500ms—the camera nearly became a strobe light.

The Naming Crisis

Initially, I named my API get_image_list.
A few weeks later, even I had no clue what it did.

A New Lens on Life: When Tech Becomes Daily Ritual

The web console made this system part of my life:

  • ☕ Morning coffee ritual: Wake up with the latest time-lapse visuals.
  • 🌱 Plant growth journal: Weekly recaps via the “Time Tunnel.”
  • 🖼️ Family time machine: Cast time-lapse memories during gatherings.

An Invitation to Makers

Building this isn’t hard:

1
2
3

# ----- Essentials -----

# Hardware: Raspberry Pi / any Linux device + webcam
# Image processing: Python + OpenCV
# Frontend: HTML + JavaScript + CSS
# Backend: PHP

Each module is like a LEGO block—ready to be customized, expanded, or swapped.

The warmth of technology lies in how we use it to illuminate and document life. I hope you too can open your own “window of time” and watch your story unfold.
